Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Foreign Affairs Ministry urges Ghanaian travellers to Côte d’Ivoire to register online 24 hours before arrival Source : Prince Adu-Owusu 19 November 2026 7:02pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has urged Ghanaian travellers heading to Côte d’Ivoire, including those transiting through the country, to complete a mandatory online registration at least 24 hours before arrival.
The requirement, introduced by the Ivorian government, is part of measures to strengthen public health surveillance amid concerns over the threat of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD).
In a statement issued on Thursday, November 19, the Ministry said the measure was announced by Côte d’Ivoire’s National Institute of Public Hygiene (INHP) on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.
Under the new arrangement, affected travellers must complete administrative and health-related formalities online and obtain a Health Pass containing a QR code before travelling.
The Ministry explained that travellers must visit the official registration platform, complete the online form with their personal identification details, travel dates and intended destination or place of stay, and submit the information for validation.
After completing the process, travellers must download the generated Health Pass and present the QR code to relevant authorities at Ivorian entry points.
The Ministry advised travellers to complete the process well ahead of departure, stressing the need to ensure that the Health Pass had been successfully generated and downloaded before starting their journey.
It warned that failure to present the required Health Pass or QR code “may result in refusal of entry into Côte d’Ivoire”.
Travellers experiencing technical difficulties or requiring clarification on the registration process have been advised to contact the relevant support service through the Contact section of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' website.
The Ministry urged Ghanaians intending to travel to or transit through Côte d’Ivoire to take note of the requirement and comply with it “to avoid inconvenience at the country's entry points”.
